solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Governor cried 'Rot!' when upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone in charge dismisses an idea with a contemptuous 'Rot!' while in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' shuffles the letters of CRIED and ROT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor of a company or school board is one who directs it, a synonym in the sense of a manager.

clue.text: Raffle that sees no one winning

definitions.meaning: a prize lottery, where tickets are pulled out
a game or match ending level, with neither side victorious

explanation.surface: A lottery in which, oddly, nobody takes the prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a lottery where tickets are pulled from a hat and a tied result in a contest.

clue.text: Strengthening for building material is under control

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed under another comes after it in the grid

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, hence control in general
cement is a material used in building

explanation.surface: A note about a material used to strengthen a structure being kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is under' places FOR and CEMENT below REIN, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcement is the act of making something stronger, so a noun of strengthening.

clue.text: Governing Conservative being nasty on the internet

parts.note: Con. is the standard abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
trolling is posting deliberately offensive messages online

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who runs things is abusive online.
explanation.definitionFit: Governing and directing both mean exercising authority over something, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Devices in pubs for scientific study

definitions.meaning: measuring devices fixed to upturned spirit bottles behind a bar
the branch of physics dealing with light and vision

explanation.surface: Pub equipment examined as a subject of research.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs an optic is a device on an upside-down bottle that dispenses an exact measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both bar dispensers for spirits and the physics of light, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Boss wants some in vexatious TU dismissed

indicators.note: some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An employer seeks the removal of some troublesome trade union members.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Boss wants' as the definition, but 'wants' is a link word; the definition is 'Boss' alone. TU is a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or ornament, as on a shield, and a stud is the same kind of projection.

clue.text: In certain plays I screamed — I got apoplectic

indicators.note: apoplectic means furious and out of control, so the letters of the words before it are thrown about

explanation.surface: A theatregoer reports shrieking with rage during some performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apoplectic' rearranges the letters of I SCREAMED I GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragicomedies are dramas blending sad and comic elements, so particular kinds of stage work.

clue.text: Intended journalist should turn up, endorsed

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for editor, a journalist
to endorse a cheque or document is to sign it

explanation.surface: A reporter is meant to arrive and give approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should turn up' flips ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something designed is done on purpose, deliberately planned, so meant or intended.

clue.text: Pakistani maybe and a second man from Scotland?

parts.note: Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Is a person from Pakistan also a second Scotsman?
explanation.definitionFit: Pakistan lies in South Asia, so a Pakistani is an example of someone from that continent.

clue.text: Aunt so troubled about cat initially getting birds

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the next piece
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of these words are stirred up
initially points to the first letter of the word cat

explanation.surface: An aunt is upset when her cat goes after birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' makes TOUANS from AUNT SO; 'about' wraps that around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Toucans are tropical birds with huge colourful bills, examples of the general class.

clue.text: Notable pups running, bound to keep going for ever

definitions.text: bound to keep going for ever

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Famous puppies racing about seem to have endless energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impossible to halt is certain to continue indefinitely.

clue.text: In predicting, ignore facts foolishly

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters of the two words before it are put in a silly order

explanation.surface: A warning against making predictions while disregarding evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Forecasting is estimating future events, so a synonym of foretelling.

clue.text: Insect given a hit went berserk

indicators.note: going berserk is running wild, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bug that was swatted flew into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went berserk' rearranges A HIT WENT. A white ant is a termite.
explanation.definitionFit: A white ant is the popular name for a termite, a wood-eating insect.

clue.text: Proclaim this female a lady regularly

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a female

indicators.note: regularly points to every other letter of lady

explanation.surface: An announcement that this woman is a lady of rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to announce it publicly, as a royal messenger once did.

clue.text: Sullen little Maureen rebelled

parts.note: Mo is a pet form of the name Maureen
to rise up is to rebel, so rose means rebelled

explanation.surface: A sulky young Maureen staged a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose and sullen both describe a gloomy, bad-tempered silence, a synonym.

clue.text: Manage to convey composer's sound

indicators.note: sound says the composer's name is taken as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Handel was the German-born composer of Messiah

explanation.surface: Coping with transmitting the noise a composer made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' gives a word pronounced like HANDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle goods is to deal with and carry them, as a porter or shipping agent does.

clue.text: New York — no small temptation for Adam?

definitions.meaning: a nickname for the American city
a large fruit, like the one Eve offered Adam in Eden

explanation.surface: New York presented as a vast lure like the forbidden fruit of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's famous nickname is literally a large fruit, which in Genesis tempted Adam.

clue.text: Given payment and something to eat

definitions.meaning: food, especially for animals or babies

explanation.surface: Someone receives wages and a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as fee'd it means paid a charge; as one word it is food for livestock or infants.

clue.text: Old archdeacon comes in to be repaid

indicators.note: comes in says one piece enters another

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon in the Church of England

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric arrives to receive his money back.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England an archdeacon is addressed as 'the Venerable', hence the short form; 'comes in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenged means paid back for a wrong, a figurative sense of repaid.

clue.text: Any number may tuck into cheese that's salty

definitions.note: a phrase for a salty thing, standing for a noun

indicators.note: tuck into means go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: Anyone can eat cheese, which tastes salty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may tuck into' places N inside BRIE; 'tuck into' looks like eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is heavily salted water used for pickling, so a thing defined by saltiness.

clue.text: Wee drinks for little kiddies

definitions.meaning: small measures of spirits, as of whisky

explanation.surface: Small drinks served to young children.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both small shots of liquor and very young children.

clue.text: Free to be given to a new tenant?

explanation.surface: A property is to be handed, perhaps free, to a fresh occupant.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed from captivity is one sense; read with a hyphen it means let out on a fresh lease.
